academicTarget: Use equal-groups structure to identify the unknown position, solve missing factors, and recognize multiple valid factor-pair arrays for a known total.
scope: Equal-groups relationship: number of groups x size of each group = total, within festival contexts of LAB-MATH-C.
Naming the unknown position (groups unknown, group size unknown, or total unknown) before any computation.
Missing-factor equations of the form ___ x 8 = 48, factors 3-9, products to 56.
Equal-sharing group size from a known total and known number of equal rows or groups (e.g., 40 flags in 5 equal rows).
Generating more than one valid factor-pair array for a known total (e.g., 36 stage lights).
Total-unknown items retained only as contrast to force discrimination between multiplying and finding a missing factor.

outOfScope: Formal long division, remainders, or division notation as a computational algorithm to be taught.
Fractions, area measurement, or multi-step problems combining operations.
Fact-fluency drill or timed recall as an instructional target; computation is assumed intact and used only as an anchor.
Non-festival contexts outside the LAB-MATH-C assignment frame.
authorityLimits: This charter defines academic scope and evidence only. It authors no questions, mechanics, visuals, themes, rewards, libraries, or HTML.
No format or modality preference may be asserted for this child; the four engagement events are activity-level facts only.
Upstream academic target and assignment text are immutable and were not altered.
childFacingTone: Child-facing language must be direct and confident. Recorded uncertainty stays in this charter and never appears as hedging to the learner.
dignity: Frame the gap as a specific habit to correct (naming the unknown), never as a deficit in the child's mathematical ability.
Do not label the learner; describe the behavior and the item type.

assumptions.decision: Treat the weakness as a single scoped failure to identify and solve the unknown position rather than a general multiplication deficit, and expect it to surface on LAB-MATH-C items 2, 3, and 8.
assumptions.uncertainty: Baseline observation 2 shows a correct unassisted missing-factor response, which is inconsistent with a uniform missing-factor weakness. The gap may be narrower than stated, possibly limited to contextual/array items rather than bare equations.
falsifyingEvidence: Learner answers items 2 and 3 correctly and unassisted while failing total-unknown items 1 and 5.
Errors appear on computation of known facts (items 1, 5) as often as on unknown-position items.
Learner produces multiple correct factor pairs for 36 without prompting, showing item 8 is not part of the same weakness.

assumptions.decision: Require the learner to name which quantity is unknown before computing on every in-scope item, in preference to additional undifferentiated practice.
assumptions.uncertainty: The comparative claim that naming beats undifferentiated practice is not supported by a controlled contrast in the supplied evidence; it is a plausible mechanism, not a demonstrated effect size.
falsifyingEvidence: Naming the unknown is done correctly but the subsequent operation choice is still wrong at a similar rate.
Substitution errors persist unchanged across items after the naming step is enforced.
Learner names the unknown correctly only after computing, indicating the step is post-hoc labeling.

assumptions.decision: Treat multiplication computation, array reading, and equal-groups story interpretation as intact and use them as contrast anchors, not instructional targets.
assumptions.uncertainty: Intactness rests on single unassisted baseline items per skill on previously practiced content; durability under novel festival contexts is untested.
falsifyingEvidence: Errors on total-unknown items 1 or 5 at a rate comparable to unknown-position items.
Misreading a 4-by-9 array when writing the two equations for item 4.
Selecting B or C on item 6, indicating story interpretation is not intact.

assumptions.decision: Anticipate and monitor over-application of the new rule: after instruction on the unknown position, some genuinely total-unknown items will be answered by dividing.
assumptions.uncertainty: Supported by a single prediction-support record; the magnitude and persistence of the over-generalization are unknown and it may be transient.
falsifyingEvidence: Total-unknown items 1 and 5 remain correct at baseline rates throughout the program.
Any division responses on total-unknown items are self-corrected before submission.
Over-application appears on total-unknown items before any unknown-position instruction, indicating a pre-existing pattern.

assumptions.decision: Assert no durable format or modality preference for this learner; the four engagement events constrain nothing about presentation and must not be used to justify a route.
assumptions.uncertainty: Four activity-level events with divergent ratings cannot separate format effect from content, novelty, or session-order effects.
falsifyingEvidence: Repeated cross-session engagement or accuracy differences that hold when content difficulty is matched across formats.
Learner explicitly and consistently requests one route across multiple sessions.
Replay behavior concentrates on one format after controlling for recency.

assumptions.decision: Treat generating multiple distinct factor pairs for a known total (item 8, 36 lights) as an in-scope target skill, distinct from computing a single product.
assumptions.uncertainty: One failed baseline item establishes that only one pair was produced; it does not distinguish inability to generate pairs from stopping early once a task was judged complete.
falsifyingEvidence: Learner produces two or more distinct valid arrays for 36 when simply asked to continue.
Failure is limited to drawing/representation rather than identifying valid pairs.
Learner lists multiple pairs verbally but records only one.

representativeLearningResponsibility.statement: Before computing, the learner names which quantity is unknown (number of groups, size of each group, or total) and then chooses multiplying or finding a missing factor accordingly.
representativeLearningResponsibility.rationale: This is the single behavior that separates the observed substitution error from intact computation, and it is the one responsibility that generalizes across items 2, 3, and 8 while protecting the intact total-unknown items 1 and 5.
representativeLearningResponsibility.successCriterion: Across in-scope items, the learner names the unknown position before computing and selects the correct operation on unknown-position items, without regressing on total-unknown contrast items.

progression: Stage 1 - Anchor: total-unknown equal-groups items (7 teams x 6 children; 3 booths x 8 cups twice) used to confirm computation and story interpretation are intact and to establish the three-quantity frame.
Stage 2 - Name the unknown: across mixed items, the learner states which of the three quantities is missing before any calculation, with no operation required yet.
Stage 3 - Group size unknown in context: 40 flags in 5 equal rows and parallel festival contexts; the learner names the unknown, then finds the missing factor using a known fact.
Stage 4 - Missing factor in equation form: ___ x 8 = 48 and siblings within factors 3-9, connecting the bare equation to the equal-groups story.

Stage 5 - Discrimination: interleave total-unknown and unknown-factor items so the learner must choose between multiplying and finding a missing factor; explicitly monitor over-application of division to total-unknown items.
Stage 6 - Multiple factor pairs: for a known total (36 lights), generate and justify more than one equal-row array, then state why each pair is valid.
evidenceRequiredNext: Per-item record of whether the unknown position was named before computing and whether it was named correctly, for every in-scope item.

Unassisted accuracy on group-size-unknown items (item 2 type) separated from unassisted accuracy on bare missing-factor equations (item 3 type), to test whether AL-D1's gap is uniform or context-specific.
Count and validity of distinct factor pairs produced for a known total, before and after any prompt to continue, to separate inability from early stopping (AL-D6).
Rate of division responses on genuinely total-unknown items (items 1 and 5 type) measured before and after unknown-position instruction, to test AL-D4 over-application.
Accuracy on array reading (item 4) and equal-groups story selection (item 6) to confirm or falsify the intact-anchor assumption AL-D3 under novel contexts.
Assistance level and exposure status recorded per item, so correctness is not credited to scaffolded or previously practiced responses.
Route or format used per session paired with difficulty-matched accuracy, recorded only to test AL-D5, not to select a presentation.
